alignments.note: `ἀσχημονέω` rendered by the light-verb frame *doth behave itself unseemly*, discontinuous across *not* (rule 15); head on the meaning-bearing *unseemly*, *behave* being the support verb and *doth* the auxiliary (rule 17).
The reflexive genitive `ἑαυτῆς` is a source word able to take the English possessive, so it displaces the substantival article's determiner and the article realizes nothing (rules 20, 54).

Reflexive possessive rendered by the two-word *its own*; head on *own*, the word realizing the reflexive force, on the reasoning rule 107 applies to a two-word emphatic. Heading on *its* remains defensible.
Passive verb with its copula, discontinuous across *not* (rules 9, 15); head on the lexical verb.

`λογίζομαι` rendered by the support-verb frame *taketh … account of*, discontinuous across *not* (rule 15); head on the meaning-bearing *account* (rule 17). The *of* stays inside this unit rather than riding to the object: `τὸ κακόν` is accusative, which English realizes with no preposition, so the *of* is licensed by the frame's own supplied noun *account* and belongs to what licenses it (rules 27, 106). Giving the *of* to `κακόν` as an *of + noun* rendering under rule 21 remains the reading the corpus takes for a genitive or dative, and is why this unit is worth checking.

The ASV writes no determiner for *evil*, so the article has nothing to anchor and is its own unit (rule 23). This is unaffected by where the *of* goes, an accusative article having no case preposition to carry in any event (rule 21).
Substantival adjective standing bare as the verb's accusative object; head on *evil* (rules 17, 106).

review_notes: The only change from the accepted alignment is t016 (*of*), which moves from the `κακόν` unit into the `λογίζεται` unit. Every status and every head is unchanged, `τό` remains `unrepresented`, and the BSB disagreement recorded against s005 is untouched.
`τὰ ἑαυτῆς` is still split: the article is `unrepresented` because the reflexive pronoun, unlike rule 47's `ἴδιος`, can itself say whose, so it carries *its own* (rules 20, 54).
Each of the four negatives is an ordinary `οὐ` aligned to its own *not*; no negative indefinite stands anywhere in the verse, so rules 41 and 59 are not in question.

The verse now treats both of its support-verb frames alike, keeping *doth behave itself unseemly* and *taketh … account of* whole inside their verbs, which is rule 24's habit applied within one verse.
